title: SDK Resilience & Compatibility Playbook: resumable streams, deterministic pagination, and retry contracts
creator: Asha Patel
description: This PRD captures cross-language SDK requirements for pagination, retry semantics, streaming APIs, and compatibility guarantees. The goal is to define a developer-friendly, language-consistent contract for clients (Python/TS/Go) that supports resumable streams, deterministic pagination cursors, clear retry idempotency expectations, and a migration path for older clients.
context: We observed multiple customer incidents where streaming connections terminated mid-response and client libraries could not resume; separate SDKs implemented divergent cursor semantics (offset vs opaque cursor) and retry backoff defaults causing unexpected duplicates or dropped requests. Platform teams are releasing runtime features (prefix caching, resumable tokens) that require client contract alignment. This ticket standardizes the client-side contract and acceptance criteria so SDKs can be implemented consistently across languages.
scope_changes: Initial scope limited to API surface and docs; expanded to include reference client behavior, interop test vectors, and migration helpers (compat adapter in SDKs). Excludes UI console changes and server-side kernel scheduling logic.
requirements: 1) Pagination: define a single canonical cursor format (opaque base64 JSON with fields: model, route, offset, seq, signature) and fallback rules for offset-based requests.

2) Resumeable Streaming: server will emit optional resume_token in stream footer every N messages. SDKs must automatically persist resume_token and provide resume API that replays from token position with at-most-once semantics when supported.

3) Retry semantics: default retry policy is exponential backoff with jitter (base 200ms, max 10s, attempts 5). Idempotency requirements: non-idempotent endpoints require explicit idempotency_key param; SDKs should surface helper to generate/parse keys.

4) Streaming backpressure and cancellation: SDKs must expose an async iterator (or language equivalent) with a cancel()/close() hook that cleanly signals server to release resources; streaming client must not auto-retry on client-cancel.

5) Compatibility: minor server behavior changes must be backward-compatible (forward-agnostic cursors). SDKs must detect server protocol_version and adapt feature flags (e.g., resume_token presence, cursor schema).
6) Observability hooks: SDKs expose hooks for latency, bytes-in/out, and token usage per request to feed Redwood Console telemetry (opt-in by default).
7) Error taxonomy: SDKs map platform errors to canonical exceptions/types: transient (retryable), permanent (no-retry), conflict (requires user action).
8) Spec docs & test vectors: single PRD-based canonical docs page + machine-readable fixtures for interop tests across Python/TS/Go.
non_goal: Implementing server-side resume storage for legacy queries is not included. Low-level kernel/runtime optimizations are out of scope. SDK language idiomatic wrappers beyond the compatibility surface are deferred to follow-up tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A. Canonical pagination cursor RFC published in docs repo and linked from SDK readmes.
B. Each SDK (python, typescript, go) implements: cursor-based list APIs, resume_token persistence and resume() method, idempotency_key helper, and standard retry/backoff defaults.

C. Integration test matrix (fixtures) exists and passes in CI for: pagination cursor rotation, streaming mid-stream resume, retry on transient network failure, and client-cancel no auto-retry. Tests must include both opaque cursor and legacy offset fallback scenarios.
D. SDK changelogs include migration notes and compatibility adapter for older clients that only understand offset cursors.
E. Performance: default retry/backoff does not increase 95th percentile latency by more than 5% for successful requests under normal load (verified in staging harness).
F. Docs: example snippets for Python/TS/Go showing list iteration, resume flow, idempotency usage, and cancellation.
G. Platform: server-side advertises protocol_version in response headers; at least two supported versions tested (v1 legacy offset, v2 opaque cursor + resume_token).
rollout_plan: 1) Publish RFC and docs (week 0). 2) Implement interop fixtures and run against mock server (week 1-2). 3) Land SDK changes behind feature flags with CI gating (week 3). 4) Gradual release: patch TS/Go clients first (most customer usage), then Python. 5) Monitor errors/telemetry and flip defaults after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
migration_notes: Provide a compatibility adapter that accepts offset queries and translates to opaque cursor on first read; adapter returns resume_token for subsequent calls. Provide deprecation schedule for offset-only support with 90-day notice. Include sample migration script for customers with custom fetch loops.
api_examples:
Python example: for item in client.list_items(cursor=None): process(item)
# on interruption: token = client.last_resume_token()
# resume: for item in client.list_items(resume_token=token): process(item)

TS example: const it = client.listItems(); for await (const item of it) { process(item) }
// resume: const it = client.listItems({ resumeToken })
links: Related tickets: ENG-4821 (streaming infra), PM-16482 (client api specs)
review_feedback: Design review (Sofia Müller): prefer opaque cursor to avoid migration complexity; accept offset fallback only as compatibility shim.
Security (Rahul Singh): no sensitive payloads in resume_token; token must be HMAC-signed and short-lived (24h).
Infra (Maya Johnson): advise server limit of resume_token retention to reduce storage blast radius; recommend TTL of 72h for persisted resumes.
qa_checks: Unit tests for cursor encode/decode across SDKs.
E2E test simulating mid-stream network drop and successful resume.
Load test with default retry policy verifying latency/regression thresholds.
Backward-compat test against v1 server behavior (offset-only).
